title: REVTURN on the S9: grblHAL lathe controller with FPGA step generation
summary: Rev's REVTURN lathe firmware (grblHAL) running on the S9: the grblHAL core as a Linux program, its step interrupt played back by the FPGA with 10 ns timing (2048-tick queue), plus hardware inputs with an instant e-stop / hard-limit stop, a probe position latch, spindle PWM and the C spindle stepper (ramped NCO for M3/M4). Serves the REVTURN lathe screen and answers as revturn.local. by JMSCNC, makers of RotatoCAM.
quickstart: Load orphan_revturn. The screen opens on port 8000: http://revturn.local:8000/lathe.html
gSender / ioSender: connect by Network (Telnet) to revturn.local, port 23.
Outputs (3.3 V, buffer to 5 V for the drivers): J6 = X step/dir + Z step/dir, J7 = C step/dir (W step/dir: not used yet), J8 pin 5 = enable. Wiring: s9/README.md in the REVTURN repo.
Inputs (switch to GND): J9 = limit X, limit Z, probe, e-stop; J1 = feed hold, cycle start, reset, limit W.
Settings are grblHAL's ($$), saved on the board. Bench tested, not yet run on the real lathe: test unloaded first.

slots.1: REVTURN step generator: tick-stream + segment modes, inputs, hard stop, probe latch, PWM, C spindle NCO
